prologue_start.001: Your memory will be returned at 00:25.
prologue_start.003: No sender. No number. Just the two lines, glowing in the dark of a room that still has half-unpacked boxes in the corner.
prologue_start.005: It has been years since anyone said that name out loud. Longer since you did.
prologue_start.007: Whoever sent it already knows. The message just wants to hear it from you.
prologue_start.008: {{playerName}}. The phone accepts it without comment.
prologue_start.010: Curiosity has never once in your life been a good enough reason to go out at midnight.
prologue_start.013: Mapo. A narrow building behind a laundromat. Permanently closed, according to the map.
prologue_start.014: Closed places don't send messages. You go to find out why this one did.
prologue_start.017: That is somehow worse than no answer. You go.
prologue_alley.001: The laundromat is still open. It is always still open. Its light spills out across the wet alley like somebody left a door unlocked for the whole street.
prologue_alley.002: Behind it: four storeys of grey brick, one window lit on the ground floor, and a sign you haven't read in a very long time.
prologue_alley.003: STUDIO 25. The 2 still hangs slightly crooked.
prologue_alley.004: You spent one winter behind that front desk. Sixteen, new in the city again, handing out sign-up forms and pencils to people who wanted to talk to their future selves.
prologue_alley.005: You left in spring. You always left in spring.
prologue_alley.006: The vending machine by the door is still humming. Of course it is.
prologue_alley.008: It rolls down the chute cold and sweet, exactly as bad for you as you remember.
prologue_alley.010: The can is almost too hot to hold. You hold it anyway.
prologue_alley.012: It is bitter and it is warm and it is exactly what one in the morning deserves.
prologue_alley.014: It tastes purple. Some things are not meant to be improved upon.
prologue_alley.015: You are not the only one here.
prologue_meet.001: Under the awning, out of the rain, eight young men are having what looks like a very serious argument in very quiet voices.
prologue_meet.002: — I'm just saying, if it were a scam, it would ask for money. It didn't ask for money.
prologue_meet.003: Maybe it's the kind of scam that asks for money *later*.
prologue_meet.004: Or maybe it's a surprise party! A really late one. For all of us. At the same time.
prologue_meet.005: Nobody has a birthday today, Hyunjun.
prologue_meet.006: That's what makes it a surprise.
prologue_meet.007: One of them — tall, pink hair gone soft in the damp — sees you and stops mid-sentence.
prologue_meet.009: Did you— wait. Sorry. Did you get a weird message too?
prologue_meet.011: That's the one! Guys, it's not just us!
prologue_meet.014: Hold up your phone so he can see the screen.
prologue_meet.015: Same words. Same time. Okay, that's officially creepy. Cool-creepy.
prologue_meet.016: All eight of them turn to look at you, the way a group of friends turns to look at the one stranger at the party.
prologue_meet.017: So that makes nine of us. Nine people, one closed building, zero explanations. I love it.
prologue_meet.018: You don't love it. You're nervous. You talk more when you're nervous.
prologue_meet.019: I talk more when I'm *happy*. And when I'm nervous. Those overlap a lot.
prologue_meet.020: The oldest-looking of them — sea-blue hair, a long grey coat, a pencil tucked behind one ear like he forgot it was there — gives you a small nod.
prologue_meet.021: Sorry. We should say who we are.
prologue_names.002: Songha. I'm the one who's going to figure out what this is.
prologue_names.003: Daniel! I'm the one who's going to press every button while he figures it out.
prologue_names.004: Hyunjun. You already met me. I was the loud one.
prologue_names.005: The tallest one spins a half-turn on the wet pavement, mostly to see if he can, and lands it.
prologue_names.006: Justin. Hi. That was on purpose.
prologue_names.008: Everything I do is on purpose.
prologue_names.009: I'm Charlie! Youngest. Which means if anything goes wrong it's automatically not my fault.
prologue_names.010: A neat one in a charcoal cardigan inclines his head, polite in a way that feels like a habit and a kindness at once.
prologue_names.011: I'm Haruta. It's nice to meet you. Even if the circumstances are… a little strange.
prologue_names.012: The last one hasn't said anything yet. Black hair, a faint blue shine to it under the streetlight. Quiet in a way that isn't shy, exactly. Watchful.
prologue_names.013: He's looking at the can in your hand. Then at your fingers, which are, you realise, trembling a little from the rain.
prologue_names.017: He doesn't say anything. He just steps sideways so you're further under the awning, out of the wind, and takes the draughty spot himself.
prologue_names.020: It's the first time you've seen him smile. It's small and it's gone quickly, like he caught himself doing it.
prologue_names.023: He believes you, or pretends to. Either way, he doesn't ask twice. That's its own kind of kindness.
prologue_names.025: {{playerName}}. Nice. Welcome to the club of people who got a creepy message and came anyway.
prologue_names.026: Did you know this place before? We did. Some of us, anyway. It used to rent out rooms really cheap.
prologue_names.027: "I used to work here. The front desk. A long time ago."
prologue_names.028: Really? Then you might know more than us.
prologue_names.029: I know where they kept the spare pencils.
prologue_names.032: Everybody's been here before, apparently. That's the weird part.
prologue_door.001: Behind you, the lock on the door of Studio 25 turns over by itself.
prologue_door.002: The door swings inward, one slow inch. Warm light spills out onto the step — not the yellow of old bulbs, but something paler. Bluer. Moving, a little, like light under water.
prologue_door.003: Nope. No. Absolutely not. That is how every horror movie starts.
prologue_door.004: Not every one. Some of them start with a dinner party.
prologue_door.006: If it's a horror movie, the tall one survives. That's a rule. I'm going first.
prologue_door.007: He doesn't go first. Nobody does. For a moment nine people stand in the rain looking at an open door, and the laundromat dryers turn and turn behind you.
prologue_door.009: You don't know why you do it. Maybe because it's the one place in this city you ever belonged to, for one winter. Maybe because somebody has to.
prologue_door.011: "Rock, paper, scissors for who goes first?"
prologue_door.012: Oh, you're my kind of person.
prologue_door.013: Daniel loses. Loudly. He goes through the door with his hands up like a hostage, and the rest of you follow him in, laughing.
prologue_door.015: It's Hanbi who moves, in the end. He glances back at you — *okay?* — and you nod, and he steps inside, and the rest follow him the way people follow someone steady.
prologue_lobby.001: The lobby of Studio 25 looks exactly like your memory of it, if your memory had been left in a drawer for years.
prologue_lobby.002: The front desk. The sagging sofas. The corkboard of old flyers. And the Archive Wall — hundreds of little glass-fronted boxes, floor to ceiling, each one holding somebody's letter to their future self.
prologue_lobby.003: It is 00:24 and fifty seconds, and every one of those boxes is beginning to glow.
prologue_lobby.005: It is 00:25. The Final Return has begun.
prologue_lobby.006: Nine recipients present. Thank you for coming. Most people do not read their messages.
prologue_lobby.008: It's a system. Some kind of speaker array. It has to be.
prologue_lobby.009: I am ECHO. I am the archive of the Future Letter Project. I am also, as of 05:00 this morning, retired.
prologue_lobby.011: The building's lease ends at dawn. My power will be cut at 05:00. Before that, I am returning the records I was built to keep.
prologue_lobby.012: RECORD 01 through RECORD 08 belong to the recipients present. Owners: Hanbi. Hamin. Songha. Charlie. Hyunjun. Haruta. Justin. Daniel.
prologue_lobby.013: Wait — we *all* sent stuff to this thing? I don't remember sending anything!
prologue_lobby.014: I do. Sort of. A video? I was like… sixteen.
prologue_lobby.015: Each record will be reconstructed on request. Records open only with their owner's consent. Unclaimed records will be deleted at 05:00.
prologue_lobby.016: The word *deleted* lands softly and stays there.
prologue_lobby.018: Eight records contain the same unresolved subject. I have not been able to identify them. I have tried for some time.
prologue_lobby.019: Recipient {{playerName}}, you are the ninth. Your presence was required.
prologue_lobby.023: …Okay. Yeah. You look about as confused as we are.
prologue_lobby.027: Look at the glowing wall instead of at them.
prologue_lobby.028: One of the boxes near the bottom glows a little brighter than the rest. You don't know why you notice it. You look away.
prologue_rule.001: Okay. Okay okay okay. New plan.
prologue_rule.002: Nobody knows what's going on. There's a building that talks. We have until five a.m. So—
prologue_rule.004: So we *stop being polite*. We are way past "nice to meet you." We're… stuck-in-a-talking-building friends now. Talk comfortably. Everybody. You too, {{playerName}}.
prologue_rule.006: Wait, can I? I'm the youngest. Can I talk comfortably to everyone? This is huge for me.
prologue_rule.009: I think I'll… stay polite a little longer. If that's okay. It's easier for me. At first.
prologue_rule.011: The two gentlemen of Studio 25. Fine. Respect. But I'm wearing you both down by three a.m.
prologue_rule.012: Recipients may leave at any time. The door is not locked. It was never locked.
prologue_rule.013: The Memory Rooms are on the second floor. Please look around. Please talk to each other. I have found that helps.
prologue_rule.014: Somewhere upstairs, eight doors hum awake at once.
act1_gather.001: The Archive Wall brightens, all at once, the way a room goes quiet when someone taps a glass.
act1_gather.002: One by one, the others drift in from the corners of the lobby. Hyunjun is still holding half a conversation with nobody. Justin is still mid-spin.
act1_gather.003: Recipients. Thank you. All nine of you have now spoken to each other.
act1_gather.006: I made an estimate. It was pessimistic. I am pleased to be wrong.
act1_gather.007: It's pleased. The building has feelings. Great. Love that.
act1_gather.008: I will now explain the rules of the night. There are not many. I have kept them short.
act1_gather.009: On the second floor is the Hall of Doors. There are eight doors. Each door is one record.
act1_gather.010: Each record opens only with its owner's consent. Nobody else can open it for them. Not even me.
act1_gather.011: A door will not open because someone else is curious.
act1_gather.012: Okay, that's actually kind of nice. Polite building.
act1_gather.014: Each room also requires Recipient {{playerName}} to be present.
act1_gather.015: For the second time tonight, eight heads turn towards you. It is less alarming the second time. Only slightly.
act1_gather.016: Wait. What's happening? Why do they have to come?
act1_gather.019: That's not an answer. That's the question with a full stop on it.
act1_gather.020: Yes. I will give a better answer when I have one. I am still looking.
act1_gather.021: So {{playerName}} is, like, the special guest. At all eight parties. That's a lot of parties.
act1_gather.022: Or the rooms need a reference point. A second witness. Something to reconstruct around.
act1_gather.025: Okay, {{playerName}}. How do you feel about being everyone's plus-one?
act1_gather.026: "I've been dragged to worse things at one in the morning."
act1_gather.028: This morning I thought I'd be asleep.
act1_gather.029: Oh, that's so much worse. You're right. This is better.
act1_gather.030: "I don't know why it's me. But if you want me there, I'll come."
act1_gather.031: …Yeah. Okay. That's a good answer. I was hoping for a funny one, but that's better.
act1_gather.032: Shrug, and look up towards the stairs.
act1_gather.033: Whatever is up there, it has been waiting longer than you have. You can wait with it a little.
act1_gather.034: That's a shrug of acceptance. I'm counting it.
act1_gather.035: The mood in the lobby shifts. Not heavier. Just more careful, the way people get before opening a letter.
act1_gather.036: I'm going first. Obviously. Is there a line? I'm starting the line.
act1_gather.037: You can't start a line with one person.
act1_gather.038: I just did. Look at it. Beautiful line.
act1_gather.039: What if mine is embarrassing, though? Like, what if I sent a video of me singing?
act1_gather.040: It's definitely embarrassing. I believe in you.
act1_gather.041: Records are not embarrassing. They are only old.
act1_gather.042: That's worse! That's so much worse!
act1_gather.044: Hanbi is sitting on the arm of the sofa with his sketchbook closed on his knees. He hasn't said anything since the word *consent*.
act1_gather.045: I think I'd… rather wait. For a bit.
act1_gather.046: Is it alright if I don't decide yet, either? I'm sorry. I'm not sure what's in mine.
act1_gather.048: He says it to the room, but he is looking at Hanbi and Haruta. Then, briefly, at you.
act1_gather.049: Tonight, or ever. That's how I understood it.
act1_gather.050: That is correct. Thank you, Recipient Hamin. You explained it more gently than I did.
act1_gather.051: Right. That's rule one, then. Nobody has to open anything.
act1_gather.052: He writes it down. He actually writes it down, in a small notebook, and underlines it twice.
act1_gather.053: Rule two: we go up together. Nobody sits in a room with a talking building alone.
act1_gather.056: Rule four. If it gets weird in there, I'm allowed to dance until it stops being weird.
act1_gather.057: That's not a rule. That's a threat.
act1_gather.058: It's both. Most good rules are.
act1_gather.059: {{playerName}}. You're really okay with this? Eight rooms. That's… a lot of other people's things.
act1_gather.060: "Only the doors someone wants opened. Only if they want me there."
act1_gather.062: He nods once, slowly, as if he is filing it somewhere safe.
act1_gather.065: At four a.m. I'm going to be asleep on that sofa. Just so everyone knows.
act1_gather.066: Hand him the pencil that's slipped from behind his ear.
act1_gather.068: He tucks it back without finishing the sentence. That seems to be the whole sentence.
act1_gather.069: The Hall of Doors is open. Please go up when you are ready. Or do not. Both are allowed.
act1_gather.070: The stairs creak exactly where they used to. The second floor is a long corridor you don't remember being this long.
act1_gather.071: Eight doors line the hall, four on each side, and every one of them is glowing faintly from the inside, like a paper lantern.
act1_gather.072: On each door, drawn in thin light, a symbol.
act1_gather.073: A wave, cresting. A city skyline at night, its windows lit. A small, round sun.
act1_gather.074: A frame of film. A pair of headphones. A single star.
act1_gather.075: A pencil, mid-line. And at the end, a rainbow, a little lopsided, as if it was drawn in a hurry.
act1_gather.076: That one's mine. The sun. I don't know how I know that. I just do.
act1_gather.077: The rainbow's mine. It's wonky. That's so accurate it's rude.
act1_gather.078: Songha stops in front of the star and doesn't say anything at all, which may be the most surprising thing he has done so far.
act1_gather.079: Eight doors. Eight people standing a careful distance from their own.
act1_gather.080: And you, in the middle of the hall, required.
hub_echo.001: RECIPIENTS PRESENT: 9. RECORDS SEALED: 8. STATUS: TALKING.
hub_echo.002: Please continue. Statistically, it is going well.
hub_echo.003: The founder placed this terminal at the height of a person sitting down. She said people tell the truth sitting down.
hub_echo.004: You are standing. That is also fine.
hub_echo.005: HALL OF DOORS: OPEN. RECORDS RETURNED: 0. RECIPIENTS WAITING: 9.
hub_echo.006: Nobody has opened a door yet. I am not rushing anyone.
hub_echo.007: I have until 05:00. For me, that is a very long time.
hub_echo.008: RECORDS RETURNED: SOME. RECORDS REMAINING: SOME. I am being vague on purpose. It seemed friendlier.
hub_echo.009: Observation: recipients laugh louder after a record is returned. I do not know why.
hub_echo.011: The founder kept a jar of pencils on the front desk. She never bought a single pencil.
hub_echo.012: They simply accumulated. She called this "community."
hub_echo.013: There are forty-one pencils in the jar tonight. One of them is Recipient Hanbi's. He has not noticed yet.
hub_echo.015: It will wait until you are. I am very good at waiting. I have had practice.
hub_echo.016: Observation: it is very quiet now. The rain has stopped. Somebody is snoring on the sofa.
hub_echo.017: I think I like this part of the night best. I did not know I could have a best part.
hamin_intro.001: Hamin is standing by the front desk holding a roll of paper towels he did not have ten minutes ago.
hamin_intro.002: He tears off three squares, folds them once, and sets them on the sofa arm beside Charlie, whose hair is still dripping onto an old flyer.
hamin_intro.003: Oh. Thanks. Wait, where did you even find these?
hamin_intro.005: How do you know there's a staff bathroom?
hamin_intro.008: Justin drifts past behind the sofa, lifts a packet of crackers out of Hyunjun's jacket pocket without breaking stride, and keeps drifting.
hamin_intro.009: He hasn't eaten since lunch. Hyunjun knows. That's why he always buys two.
hamin_intro.010: He says it quietly, to nobody in particular. Then he looks at you, and then, briefly, at the empty can you still haven't found a bin for.
hamin_intro.011: Peach iced tea. In the rain.
hamin_intro.014: You were holding it through your sleeve. It must have been very hot.
hamin_intro.015: Black coffee. At one in the morning.
hamin_intro.016: So you're planning to stay up.
hamin_intro.018: I didn't know anyone actually bought those. I thought they were for decoration.
hamin_intro.019: "Do you always take inventory of people?"
hamin_intro.021: The bin is behind the desk, by the way. Under the lost property box.
hamin_intro.024: The bin is behind the desk. If you were looking for it.
hamin_intro.025: Hand him the can, since he seems to know where it goes.
hamin_intro.026: He takes it without comment and drops it into a bin behind the desk that you would never have found.
hamin_intro.028: There's a heater under the window. It works if you hit the side twice.
hamin_intro.029: I hit it. It's on now. Just so you know.
hamin_intro.030: Did you send something here too? To the Future Letter Project?
hamin_intro.032: I think I sent the sea.
hamin_intro.033: He says it the way other people say *a postcard*.
hamin_intro.034: A recording. From Busan. I was fourteen. It seemed like a good idea at the time.
hamin_intro.036: He remembers exactly why. You can tell by how quickly he looks at the Archive Wall and then away from it.
hamin_intro.037: Also — you were humming. At the door, earlier.
hamin_intro.039: The song from the laundromat. It's been playing the same one on a loop since we got here. Probably since two thousand and ten.
hamin_intro.040: …Sorry. I notice things. I'm not keeping a list.
hamin_intro.041: He is, you suspect, keeping a list.
hamin_intro_repeat.001: The heater's still on. Charlie's mostly dry.
hamin_intro_repeat.002: Justin has eaten one cracker. That's progress.
hamin_intro_repeat.003: He delivers it like a weather report. It is, somehow, the most reassuring thing anyone has said tonight.
hamin_door.001: The second-floor hallway hums. Eight doors, each with light moving behind the frosted glass.
hamin_door.002: Downstairs, Daniel is losing an argument with the claw machine. It sounds like a long argument.
hamin_door.003: Behind Hamin's, the light rises and falls, slowly. Like breathing. Like something coming in and going out.
hamin_door.005: RECORD 02 — OWNER: HAMIN. STATUS: SEALED. AWAITING CONSENT.
hamin_door.006: It's just the sea. Four minutes of it.
hamin_door.007: You might be bored. I'm telling you in advance, so you can't say I didn't warn you.
hamin_door.008: If it's boring, you can leave halfway. I won't notice.
hamin_door.010: He isn't looking at the door. He's looking at the floor in front of it, where the light pools and pulls back.
hamin_door.011: It's fine. You can open it.
hamin_door.012: …That sounded like I was talking to a dentist.
hamin_door.013: What I mean is, I'd like you to be there. If you want to be.
hamin_door.017: He lets out a breath. It isn't quite a laugh.
hamin_door.018: Honestly, that's a relief. I was going to pretend to be calm for another ten minutes.
hamin_door.019: It's waited six years. It can wait a little longer.
hamin_room.002: Not a picture of sand. Sand, or ECHO's best guess at it — cool and fine, giving a little under each step. The hallway is gone behind you.
hamin_room.003: A beach at night. A long curve of dark water, a line of foam that keeps arriving, and far along the shore, the lights of a city that isn't Seoul.
hamin_room.004: RECORD 02 — OWNER: HAMIN. TYPE: VOICE MEMO. LENGTH: FOUR MINUTES, TWELVE SECONDS.
hamin_room.005: LOCATION: A BEACH IN BUSAN. DATE: JULY, SIX YEARS AGO. 23:41.
hamin_room.007: Hamin stands at the edge of it with his hands in his coat pockets, very still, the way people stand at the edge of cold water.
hamin_room.009: I didn't think it would smell right.
hamin_room.010: He looks up the beach, towards the seawall, where a vending machine hums in a square of white light.
hamin_room.012: The vending machine slides one metre to the left, with the faint air of something that has been corrected before and didn't enjoy it.
hamin_room.015: The unresolved subject. That's the part I don't understand.
hamin_room.016: I was alone that night. I'm fairly sure I was alone. I went there specifically to be alone.
hamin_room.019: Everyone's come out of their rooms tonight looking at you with the same face.
hamin_room.020: At this point, it would be stranger if it *wasn't* you.
hamin_room.021: He glances at you. You glance at the sea. Neither of you says the theory out loud.
hamin_room.022: We could not mention it. For a bit. Let it be a surprise.
hamin_room.023: The others came out of their rooms looking at you a bit strangely.
hamin_room.024: I didn't ask. It seemed rude.
hamin_room.026: "If it's me, I apologise in advance."
hamin_room.028: I don't know yet. That's why it's in advance.
hamin_room.030: "Whatever's in here, I'll stay for all four minutes."
hamin_room.033: Stand beside him at the edge and look at the water.
hamin_room.034: He doesn't say anything. After a moment his shoulders come down half an inch, as if he'd been holding them up for both of you.
hamin_room.035: Beginning reconstruction. Please do not step on the owner.
hamin_room.036: The light shifts. The moon moves a few degrees along the sky, as if someone nudged it with one finger.
hamin_room.037: Up the beach, a boy of fourteen sits cross-legged on the sand, holding a phone out towards the water at arm's length. Very seriously.
hamin_room.038: He is trying not to breathe too loudly. You can tell. His whole back is concentrating.
hamin_room.039: Thirty metres further along, there is a shape made of soft light. Knees pulled up. Arms around them. Shivering.
hamin_room.041: The boy looks at the phone. Then at the shape. Then at the phone again, like he's trying to work out which one is his problem.
hamin_room.042: He stops the recording. He stands up. He walks — not to the shape, but past it, up to the vending machine by the seawall.
hamin_room.043: When he comes back, he is holding a can. He holds it out at arm's length, exactly the way he held the phone.
hamin_room.046: It's hot. Corn tea. It was the only hot one.
hamin_room.049: I didn't know the sea got cold at night. We only moved here last week.
hamin_room.050: I thought beaches were a daytime thing.
hamin_room.051: It's a night thing too. Just a different one.
hamin_room.052: He sits down — not next to the light, but a polite metre away. He presses record again. He doesn't explain.
hamin_room.056: I might go to Seoul. Next year, maybe. It's a long story.

hamin_ending.032: They don't have it in cans. I asked if she could make it. She had peaches. She seemed excited, honestly.
hamin_ending.033: Less ice than normal. You were holding the can by the rim outside, so your fingers wouldn't get cold. So — less ice.
hamin_ending.034: A hot chocolate, steaming just slightly less than hot chocolate usually steams.
hamin_ending.035: I asked for it a bit cooler than normal.
hamin_ending.036: You hold hot things through your sleeve and then wait for them anyway. So I thought — skip the waiting.
hamin_ending.037: A black coffee in a heavy white cup, nothing in it, nothing beside it.
hamin_ending.038: You made a face at the can outside. But you finished it. So I think the face was about the can, not the coffee.
hamin_ending.039: I asked what beans they use. I don't know anything about beans. I nodded a lot.
hamin_ending.040: A can of grape soda, sweating a little, standing very upright in the middle of a café that does not sell anything in cans.
hamin_ending.041: They didn't have it. There's a convenience store on the corner.
hamin_ending.042: I asked if I could bring it in. She said it was the strangest thing anyone had asked her all week. I think it was a compliment.
hamin_ending.044: While you were taking your coat off.
hamin_ending.045: I said "next time". Six years ago. I don't say a lot of things. So I try to keep the ones I do.
hamin_ending.046: The sun gets the rest of the way through the window, lands on the table, and stays there, as if it's been told this is the place.
hamin_ending.047: He is watching you take the first sip. Not the drink. You. Checking it's right, the way he's checked everything all night.
hamin_ending.049: It's not a big deal, but—
hamin_ending.050: This place opens at five-thirty. Every day.
hamin_ending.052: "Tomorrow, then. And the day after that."
hamin_ending.053: …You don't have to decide the day after that right now.
hamin_ending.055: You keep doing that. Deciding things out loud before I've finished being nervous about them.
hamin_ending.056: "Are you asking me to breakfast, or reading me the opening hours?"
hamin_ending.058: …Breakfast. I'm asking you to breakfast. Songha would be proud of how long it took me to say that.
hamin_ending.059: "I unpacked the kettle last week. I think that means I'm staying."
hamin_ending.061: It's always the last thing. If the kettle's out, I'm not leaving.
hamin_ending.062: …Then I'll stop checking the exits for you.
hamin_ending.063: You have always left. New city, new school, a season and then the boxes again. You always left in spring.
hamin_ending.064: It is September. Spring is a long way off. And for the first time, you aren't counting towards it.
hamin_ending.065: On the table, his hand has ended up next to yours. Not on it. Next to it. Close enough that it's a question.
hamin_ending.066: You answer it. His fingers are still a little cold from the walk over. That's fine. You have a hot drink, or a cold one, and all morning.
hamin_ending.070: He slides the sugar over to you without being asked, even though you don't take any. Then he realises, and slides it back, and hides his face in his cup.
hamin_ending.073: …Good. I'll get the next one. Same thing?
hamin_newmem.001: A week later. The laundromat behind Studio 25 is still open, because it is always still open.

daniel_route.109: Can I say something? Not a bit. A real one.
daniel_route.111: I made the list because I thought—
daniel_route.112: If it went quiet, you'd notice there wasn't anything else. No arcade. No games. Just me, in a room.
daniel_route.113: And that's not— it's not much.
daniel_route.114: He says it to his knees. He says it without a single exclamation mark. You didn't know he owned a sentence like that.
daniel_route.115: "I came here for just you, in a room."
daniel_route.116: You can't just say that. In the dark. With no music.
daniel_route.117: I think this is the only place you can say it.

daniel_route.123: Is this okay? This. Just this?

daniel_route.127: …What do you do? When it's quiet. Wherever you live now.

daniel_route.132: Okay. Good. I mean— not good. Fair. It's fair.
daniel_route.135: It ticks. It's a good listener.
daniel_route.136: I'm going to be a good listener. Watch. Starting now.
daniel_route.141: He says it like a fact he's just checked, and found to be true.
daniel_route.143: I have one strip of film left in the reconstruction. Four frames. I would like to use it, if you would like to be in it.
daniel_route.145: Only the rain. It is in the record. I cannot take it out.
daniel_route.146: That's okay. The rain can stay.
daniel_route.147: The booth builds itself around the two of you out of soft light. The bench. The curtain. The little screen.
daniel_route.148: The rain on the roof. The same rain, applauding nobody.

daniel_route.150: The screen lights up. FOUR FRAMES. SMILE!
daniel_route.151: Oh no. It's going. Okay, okay, pose—
daniel_route.152: FRAME ONE. His hand comes up — peace sign, tongue half out — and stops halfway, like he's just remembered he doesn't have to.
daniel_route.153: He laughs at himself, and puts the hand down.
daniel_route.154: Pull a face at the camera.
daniel_route.155: FRAME TWO. You, making the worst face of your life on purpose. Daniel, staring at you, delighted and betrayed. That was supposed to be his job.
daniel_route.156: Look at him instead of the camera.
daniel_route.157: FRAME TWO. The camera catches you looking at him. It catches him catching you. Neither of you looks away in time.
daniel_route.158: Sit still and let it happen.
daniel_route.159: FRAME TWO. Two people on a bench. One of them is trying very hard not to grin, and losing.
daniel_route.160: FRAME THREE. Both of you laughing at nothing in particular, which is the best thing there is to laugh at.
daniel_route.161: The screen counts down to the last frame. Five. Four.
daniel_route.164: He turns towards you. Slowly, so you can see it coming. So you could say no.
daniel_route.167: He leans in until his forehead rests against yours. His hair is soft and ridiculous and smells faintly of the arcade.
daniel_route.168: Your hand is still in his. It has been, the whole time.
daniel_route.169: He finds your hand without looking, and asks with his thumb, and you answer the same way.
daniel_route.171: He leans back against the booth wall. After a second, his shoulder settles against yours, and stays.
daniel_route.172: He doesn't look at the camera. He looks at the curtain, and the rain, and — once, quickly, like he's checking you're still there — at you.
daniel_route.175: Nobody posing. Nobody performing. Two people on a bench, waiting out a rain that is only a memory, in no hurry at all for it to stop.
daniel_route.176: The booth prints the strip with a whirr and a small, satisfied click.
daniel_route.177: RECORD 08. FRAMES FIVE THROUGH EIGHT: APPENDED. CONDITION: DRY.
daniel_route.178: I have never added to a record before. I believe it was allowed.
daniel_route.179: Daniel holds the new strip up by one corner, like it might still be wet.
daniel_route.180: Frame one: me, quitting halfway. That's growth. Write that down.
daniel_route.181: Frame three: we look insane. Good. Correct.
daniel_route.182: And look at the last one.
daniel_route.183: That's my favourite. Again. Two for two.
daniel_route.184: The booth dims around you until it is only the room again. The radiator. The stripe of light under the door.

daniel_route.189: We got to it early. Kind of. I skipped five whole things.
daniel_route.190: Songha's going to look at this page and think I got kidnapped.
daniel_route.191: Tell him number eleven took longer than planned.
daniel_route.193: I don't want to plan anything else tonight. I just want—
daniel_route.194: Can I just want this? Is that allowed?
daniel_route.196: He lets out a breath that sounds like it has been waiting two years.
daniel_route.197: I think I'm getting better at it. Nothing. Sitting.
daniel_route.199: Don't tell anyone. I have a reputation.
daniel_route.200: All recipients: please come to the lobby. It is almost time. I would like everyone to be there.
daniel_route.202: He stands, and pulls you up by the hand, and doesn't let go of it on the stairs. Not once.
daniel_route.203: He stands, and pulls you up by the hand, and lets go a second later than he needs to.
daniel_ending.001: The Archive Wall is almost dark now. Hundreds of little glass boxes, gone quiet one by one. Only the eighth is still lit.
daniel_ending.003: Writing four frames. Then four more. Then a note in the margin: "Condition: dry."
daniel_ending.004: A small glass card slides out of a slot in the front desk that you never knew was there. It is warm, like a cup someone has just put down.
daniel_ending.005: Inside the glass: eight tiny frames. A pose. A startle. Two strangers laughing. Two strangers sitting.
daniel_ending.006: Then the new four, all the way down to the last one, where nobody is doing anything at all.
daniel_ending.007: …It's so small. Why is it so small? I thought it'd be, like, a poster.
daniel_ending.008: Is that the booth one? Let me see— oh. *Oh*. Frame eight. Hyung.
daniel_ending.009: Of course it's the booth one. I would've put money on it. I did, actually. Hyunjun owes me three thousand won.
daniel_ending.010: I said the claw machine! That's basically the same thing! It's the same *genre*!
daniel_ending.011: Frame one's great, by the way. That's a professional pose. I respect it.
daniel_ending.012: The last frame is good. Nobody would have written it like that. That's why it works.
daniel_ending.015: Daniel doesn't say anything. He holds the card up to the last light of the Archive Wall and grins at it like it just told him a secret.
daniel_ending.016: Then he turns the card round so you can see it too, and keeps it there, between the two of you, where both of you can hold an edge.
daniel_ending.017: ECHO? Thanks. For keeping it. Even wet.
daniel_ending.018: You are welcome, Recipient Daniel. It was my favourite record to be bad at.
daniel_ending.019: Also, I'd like my notebook back.
daniel_ending.020: You'll get it back! I only used one page. And a half. There's a drawing of Mr. Kim.
daniel_ending.021: Hongdae at twenty to six is a different city. Shutters down. A street sweeper humming. Two pigeons holding a meeting about a dropped triangle kimbap.
daniel_ending.022: It's a fifteen-minute walk from Studio 25 to here. Daniel made it take forty.
daniel_ending.023: He stopped at every photo booth on the way and looked inside, like he was checking on old friends.
daniel_ending.024: The others went ahead to breakfast. Hamin said he'd order for everyone. Songha said he'd order for Hamin.
daniel_ending.025: The arcade is closed. The booth outside it is a newer one — pink, with a sticker promising the best photos in Mapo.
daniel_ending.026: The awning is exactly as useless as you remember.
daniel_ending.027: You and Daniel are sitting on the step beside it. Nobody decided to. It just happened, about twenty minutes ago.
daniel_ending.028: Mr. Kim's former prisoner sits on the step between you, watching the sky go from grey to peach.
daniel_ending.029: His phone buzzes. He reads it. He doesn't answer it.
daniel_ending.031: He stands, and stretches until something in his back clicks, and pats his pockets for nothing in particular.
daniel_ending.034: You said that twenty minutes ago.
daniel_ending.036: He looks at you. Then at the street. Then he sits back down.
daniel_ending.038: You have never once in your life asked for five more minutes.
daniel_ending.039: You were always the one who knew exactly when to leave. The thank-you over the shoulder. The curtain swinging shut behind you. The rain stopping, and you going with it.
daniel_ending.040: Daniel's head comes to rest on your shoulder, heavy and warm, and his hand finds yours on the step as if it has done it a hundred times.
daniel_ending.043: Okay. Just checking. I'm going to keep checking. Forever, probably.
daniel_ending.044: Daniel's shoulder settles against yours. His knee doesn't bounce once.
daniel_ending.047: I'm not going to say anything else. Look at me. Not saying anything else.
daniel_ending.048: He doesn't fill the silence. He doesn't need to.
daniel_ending.049: The street does it for him: a shutter going up, a bike bell, a pigeon with opinions. The light coming up over Mapo like it has nowhere else to be.
daniel_ending.052: Not the ECHO kind. The normal kind.
daniel_ending.053: This counts. This is my favourite frame.
daniel_ending.054: There's no camera. He doesn't seem to mind.
daniel_newmem.001: A week later. A Tuesday, which is the least eventful day ever invented.
daniel_newmem.002: Hongdae, three in the afternoon. The pink booth by the arcade has a queue of exactly one person, and he is waving at you with both arms.
daniel_newmem.003: {{playerName}}! You came! I wasn't sure you'd— no, I was sure. I was mostly sure.
daniel_newmem.004: Okay. So. ECHO's asleep. The Future Letter Project is closed. The studio is currently full of men with drills.
daniel_newmem.005: Which means somebody has to keep the archive going. Unofficially. Me. I'm the archive now.
daniel_newmem.007: One strip. Four frames. Every week, until I run out of money, which will be soon.
daniel_newmem.008: Songha made me a spreadsheet for it. Hanbi bought me a folder. Charlie keeps asking what the folder's for.
daniel_newmem.009: The booth is exactly as narrow as the other one. Some things are just standard.
daniel_newmem.010: Frame one, pose. Frame two, pose worse. Frame three, whatever happens happens.
daniel_newmem.014: Frame one: a peace sign, and a worse peace sign.
daniel_newmem.015: Frame two: a face you will deny making.
daniel_newmem.016: Frame three: whatever happened. It's mostly elbows.
daniel_newmem.017: Frame four: two people on a bench, not doing anything, for almost the whole three seconds.
daniel_newmem.018: Then, at the very last instant, Daniel's composure breaks, and the camera catches him laughing at absolutely nothing.
daniel_newmem.019: That still counts! Nobody said nothing had to be *quiet*.
daniel_newmem.020: The machine prints two copies, still warm. He hands you one without looking at it, like it was always going to be yours.
daniel_newmem.022: I was going to say that! That's my whole line. You keep taking my lines.
daniel_newmem.023: Tuck the strip into your coat. The inside pocket, where the rain can't get it.
daniel_newmem.024: …Good. Good pocket choice. Very dry. I approve.
daniel_newmem.026: Daniel looks at the sky, then at the booth, then at you.

interlude_2.001: Four doors now. The lobby has become a kind of camp: shoes by the sofa, jackets on the backs of chairs, somebody's socks drying on the radiator.
interlude_2.002: Justin is stretching on the floor. Songha is re-reading his notebook. Charlie has built a fort out of cushions and is refusing to explain it.

interlude_2.026: I laughed so hard I had to sit down on the library floor.
interlude_2.027: So. I'm building a place where "someday" can wait for you. You leave a letter. A song. A picture. And later, you come back and argue with who you were.

interlude_2.029: …I'm told the little light means it's still recording. Goodnight, archive. Be nice to them.

interlude_3.001: Six doors. Somewhere between one room and the next, the rain stopped. Nobody noticed until the quiet became loud.
