interlude_3.037: Slowly, it develops: a blur of arms and hair and the corner of the front desk. Justin mid-fall. Hyunjun too high. Hanbi's hand on somebody's shoulder.
interlude_3.038: And you, right in it. Not at the edge. Laughing at something you can't remember now, and will not forget.
interlude_3.039: Afterwards, the lobby goes soft. People settle in twos, the way people do at three in the morning.
interlude_3.040: By the window, Hanbi and Songha are sharing one earbud each and pretending not to be tired.
interlude_3.041: I didn't plan any of this.
interlude_3.042: I know. It's been nice watching.
interlude_3.043: On the sofa, Justin gives Hyunjun the last of the shrimp crackers. Hyunjun stares at the bag like it might be a trick.
interlude_3.045: Don't make it weird. It's a limited-time offer.
interlude_3.046: Charlie has fallen asleep sitting up, his head sliding slowly onto Daniel's shoulder. Daniel, for once in his life, is holding perfectly still.
interlude_3.047: {{playerName}}. Don't make me laugh. If I laugh, he wakes up.
interlude_3.048: And if he wakes up, he's going to ask what's happening. And I don't know. I genuinely don't know any more.
interlude_3.049: He says it in a whisper, and he is smiling, and he doesn't move a single muscle.
interlude_3.050: Hamin and Haruta are side by side at the front desk, watching the photo finish developing as if it's a film that might still change its ending.
interlude_3.056: The whole room hears it. Charlie wakes up. Nobody says anything.
interlude_3.057: Not now, if you don't want. Whenever you want.
interlude_3.058: Nobody has to open anything. That goes for you too.
interlude_3.060: Soon's good. Soon's a real time. I can write that down.
interlude_3.061: "After the other doors. I'm saving the weird one for last."
interlude_3.063: Look at the photo in Hamin's hands instead.
interlude_3.064: Nine people in a square of expired film. That, at least, is a record you already know how to read.
interlude_3.065: Wait. Who gets to keep the photo? There's only one. Plus the nostril one.
interlude_3.066: I'll make a rotation. A week each, alphabetical—
interlude_3.068: …Okay. Later. We'll figure it out later.
act3_start.001: Eight doors, all of them dark now. Eight records returned. The Hall of Doors should be finished.
act3_start.002: It isn't. At the end of the corridor, where there was only wall an hour ago, there is a ninth door.
act3_start.003: It has no symbol. Just a small brass plate, the kind that used to be on the front desk, and on it a name.
act3_start.005: RECORD 09 — OWNER: {{playerName}}. TYPE: LETTER. DATE: SIX YEARS AGO. STATUS: SEALED.
act3_start.006: I did not know this record existed until 00:25. It was filed under FRONT DESK — MISC. I apologise. My filing was not always good.
act3_start.007: A letter. You wrote a Future Letter. While you worked here.
act3_start.010: It's true. You remember the desk, the forms, the pencils. You don't remember sitting down and writing one yourself.
act3_start.011: …Okay. That's allowed. It was six years ago.
act3_start.012: "Everyone who worked here had to. It was in the contract."
act3_start.014: There wasn't. There was a founder who said "you too" and pushed a form across the desk. Same thing.
act3_start.015: Look at the brass plate and say nothing.
act3_start.016: The name is in your own handwriting. Younger. Rounder. Somebody who pressed too hard with the pencil.
act3_start.017: It's the same rule. Nobody has to open anything.
act3_start.019: The owner's consent is required. I will wait. I have been waiting six years. A few more minutes will not register.
act3_start.022: That's fine. We're not going anywhere.
act3_start.023: Yeah! We'll just — stand here. In a hallway. At three-thirty in the morning. Like normal people.
act3_start.024: They do, too. Nobody checks the time. Nobody says "we've only got until five." Eight people lean on a wall and wait for you.
act3_start.025: Hyunjun starts humming something. Justin taps the beat on the radiator. It is, absurdly, comfortable.
act3_start.026: After a while, the door doesn't seem so heavy.
act3_room.001: The front desk of Studio 25, six years ago. Rain on the window. A radio somewhere playing a song that was already old.
act3_room.002: ECHO has rebuilt it from the inside out: the sign-up forms, the jar of pencils, the corkboard. A stack of moving boxes by the wall, half-taped, with a city name on each one.
act3_room.003: Busan. Seoul. Seoul again. A city abroad, the name in a different alphabet. Seoul.
act3_room.004: And at the desk, a figure of soft light. Sixteen. Sleeves too long. Writing something with a pencil pressed far too hard.
act3_room.005: The boxes have *labels*. That's so many cities.
act3_room.008: It's a strange thing to say out loud in a room made of your own past. The boxes make it look like a fact instead of a feeling.
act3_room.009: That's… that's a lot of last days.
act3_room.011: Okay, but were you good at *unpacking*?
act3_room.012: You look at the boxes. Half-taped. You don't answer, and he's kind enough to let it go.
act3_room.014: Hamin glances at the boxes, then at you, and doesn't ask anything. He just moves a little closer to where you're standing.
act3_room.016: The figure at the desk finishes writing. Folds the paper twice. Slides it into the slot — the one that sticks — and has to push it with two fingers.
act3_room.017: You too, kid. Everybody who works here writes one. Studio rules.
act3_room.018: The founder, off to one side, sleeves rolled up, laughing at something on her phone. Seo Yeonhwa. You had forgotten her voice. You had not forgotten her laugh.
act3_room.019: What if I'm not here to read it?
act3_room.020: Then it'll wait. That's what the building's for.
act3_room.021: The letter unfolds in the air in front of you, the way ECHO unfolds everything — too carefully, like it's afraid of tearing.
act3_room.022: You know the handwriting. You don't know the words until you read them.
act3_room.023: "Dear future me. I don't know where you are when you read this. I don't know what city. I've stopped guessing."
act3_room.024: "I hope you're okay. I hope you found people. I hope you stayed long enough that somebody learned how you take your drink."
act3_room.025: "I hope, by the time you read this, you've found a place you want to stay."
act3_room.026: Hanbi is the first to speak, and it isn't with words. He takes a breath in, holds it, lets it go.
act3_room.027: …That's a lot to ask of a letter.
act3_room.028: It's not asking the letter. It's asking you.
act3_room.030: It comes out steadier than you expected. Nobody rushes to fill the silence after it.
act3_room.032: Two words. He means tonight. He might mean more than tonight. He doesn't explain, and you don't ask him to.
act3_room.034: It's *so* covered. Half this building knows your order now.
act3_room.035: Hamin looks at the floor with the specific expression of somebody who has been caught remembering something.
act3_room.036: Fold the letter back up and hold it.
act3_room.037: The paper is warm, the way ECHO's things are warm. Daniel looks like he wants to say a joke and decides, visibly, not to.
act3_room.038: You don't have to answer it tonight. It's a letter. It's patient.
act3_link.002: RECORD 01 through 08 each contain one unresolved subject. RECORD 09 resolves them.
act3_link.004: The front desk folds away. In its place, a room made of other rooms.
act3_link.005: A beach at night. The last train. An airport board. A cinema seat. A doorway with a key ring on the hook. A rooftop. A lounge sofa. A photo booth.
act3_link.006: Eight rooms, stitched together at the edges like a quilt. And in every one of them, standing where the silhouette stood: a younger version of you, in a coat with sleeves too long.
act3_link.007: Subject: {{playerName}}. Appears in eight records over six years, in four cities.
act3_link.008: Encounters were brief. None exceeded one night. None were repeated. The subject was, on each occasion, about to leave.
act3_link.010: I searched for one. For some time. There is no pattern. There is no signal. There is no schedule. I am sorry if that is disappointing.
act3_link.011: No pattern. Eight times. That's — statistically, that's —
act3_link.012: It's fate. Right? That's what this is. It has to be. Nine people, one building, the same night —
act3_link.013: It's not fate. ECHO just said. It looked.
act3_link.014: ECHO's a *filing system*, hyung. It wouldn't know fate if fate walked in and asked for the wifi password.
act3_link.017: Whether it was fate. Does it change what happened?
act3_link.019: It surprises you as you say it, and then it doesn't. If it were fate, none of it would have been anyone's choice.
act3_link.020: A kid who gave a stranger a hot can on a beach. A kid who stayed on a train. A kid who said "you don't have to stop."
act3_link.021: Those were chosen. Every one of them.
act3_link.023: I'd rather have chosen it too.
act3_link.024: "If it's fate, fate has terrible timing. Six years?"
act3_link.025: Fate showed up eight times and forgot to introduce itself. Fate's a mess.
act3_link.026: To be fair. So were we. I didn't even get a name.
act3_link.027: Hyunjun says it lightly. It isn't light. Nobody pretends it is.
act3_link.029: That's the whole film, I think. Someone was there. Someone noticed. That's — that's the whole film.
act3_link.030: No plot twist. Just people. I can work with that.
act3_link.031: Songha looks at his notebook for a long moment. Then he closes it.
act3_link.032: Okay. No pattern. I'm writing down "no pattern" and I'm going to let that be an answer.
act3_link.033: Look at him. Growth. At three-forty in the morning.
act3_founder.001: One more item is attached to RECORD 09. It is not the owner's. It is the founder's. She asked that it be played "to whoever's left at the end."
act3_founder.002: You are whoever is left. Playing.
act3_founder.003: Hello. If you're hearing this, it's the last night, and ECHO's being dramatic about it. Ignore that. It gets like this.
act3_founder.004: I built this place because people kept saying "someday." Someday I'll record that song. Someday I'll tell them. Someday I'll go back.
act3_founder.005: So I gave someday a mailbox. That's all the Future Letter Project ever was. A mailbox for later.
act3_founder.006: But here's the thing I figured out too late, kids, and I want you to have it now, for free:
act3_founder.007: Archives are for keeping. People aren't.
act3_founder.008: Don't keep each other. Meet each other. Again. On purpose. That's the trick. Okay. That's the message. Somebody turn the lights off when you go.
act3_founder.010: That's the best advice I've ever gotten from a wall.
act3_founder.011: It is 03:50. Time remaining: seventy minutes.
act3_founder.012: The building is yours until then. I have no further records. I have no further rules.
act3_founder.013: Recipient {{playerName}} — you have been in eight of our memories tonight. Where would you like to be, for the ninth?
act3_choice.001: The lobby again. Everyone drifts apart the way people do at the end of a long night, not leaving — just spreading out into the building.
act3_choice.002: Somebody goes up to the roof. Somebody goes to the practice room. Somebody sits on the worst sofa in Seoul.
act3_choice.003: Seventy minutes. One building. Where do you want to be?
act4_choice.001: 04:57. Everyone is back in the lobby without anyone having called them. The building did it, somehow — or the hour did.
act4_choice.002: The Archive Wall is dark except for a soft line of light running along the front desk, like a shoreline.
act4_choice.003: It is 04:57. My power will be cut in three minutes.
act4_choice.004: I can write one record to the keepsake card. One. The card is small. I requested a larger card. Nobody replied.
act4_choice.005: Recipient {{playerName}} — you are the subject every record shares. The choice is yours. Please choose one record to preserve.
act4_choice.007: So much pressure. Historic amounts of pressure. Take your time. You have three minutes.
echo_farewell.002: Nine recipients present. Zero records unclaimed. That has never happened before.
echo_farewell.003: I was built to keep things until someone came back for them. Tonight everyone came back. I find that I do not know what to do with my hands. I do not have hands. The feeling persists.
echo_farewell.004: Thank you for opening the doors. Thank you for saying "not yet" when you needed to. I have logged those too. They were also records.
echo_farewell.005: Goodnight. Please turn off the lights when you go. She asked.
echo_farewell.006: The line of light along the desk goes out. Then the glow in the walls. Then the low hum under everything that you had stopped hearing hours ago.
echo_farewell.007: For a moment the lobby is completely dark and completely quiet, and nine people breathe in it.
echo_farewell.008: A phone torch clicks on. Hanbi's, of course.
echo_farewell.010: Was that — did the building just say goodnight? I'm never going to be normal about this.
echo_farewell.011: You were never normal about anything. That's your whole thing.
echo_farewell.012: Somewhere outside, the laundromat's sign buzzes back on. The sky in the window has gone from black to the deep blue of a bruise healing.
true_ending.001: It comes out before you've decided to say it. The way true things do.
true_ending.004: "You don't have to keep any of it. We'll keep each other."
true_ending.005: "Delete the lot. We're going to breakfast."
true_ending.007: Eight people look at you. Then at each other. Then — slowly, like a wave deciding — they start to nod.
true_ending.009: Yeah! Yes. One more of *everything*. Starting now.
true_ending.010: Step one: breakfast. I'll allow it. I'll allow it without a schedule.
true_ending.011: Wait, are we really not keeping anything? Not even the photo?
true_ending.012: We have the photo. It's in your pocket, Charlie. It's a photo.
true_ending.013: …Oh. Right. Right! We have the photo.
true_ending.014: Then it isn't an ending. It's a cut to the next scene.
true_ending.015: And the next scene has eggs in it.
true_ending.017: Recipient {{playerName}}. Nine recipients. Zero records selected for preservation.
true_ending.018: I have checked the request three times. It is consistent. Then there is nothing I need to keep.
true_ending.019: I understand now what she meant. It took me six years and one night. I was not built quickly.
true_ending.020: Meet each other again. On purpose. I will not be here to see it. That is correct. That is how it should work.
true_ending.021: Goodnight, everyone. Thank you for the new memory. I am not keeping it. I am just — holding it a moment.
true_ending.022: The lights go. The hum goes. The building becomes a building.
true_ending.023: In the dark, someone — Hyunjun, it's definitely Hyunjun — says "one more minute," and everyone laughs, and nobody moves.
true_dawn.001: Sunrise on the alley behind the laundromat. Peach light on wet brick. The STUDIO 25 sign with its crooked 2, going gold for the first and last time.
true_dawn.002: Nine people on the step, blinking at the sky like it's a rumour that turned out to be true.
true_dawn.003: The only place open at 06:40 is a kimbap shop with three tables. Nine people fit at three tables if two of them stand and Charlie sits on a crate.
true_dawn.004: Songha orders for everyone without asking, then asks everyone, then re-orders. Hanbi pays before anyone notices. Daniel notices and yells about it.
true_dawn.005: Hyung, you can't just *pay*. That's a hostile act. We were going to split it.
true_dawn.007: Okay, real question, no jokes. Same time next week?
true_dawn.008: Next week is fine. I'm writing it down. I'm not writing anything *else* down. Just the day.
true_dawn.011: Can we go somewhere with more chairs next time? Not for me. For the crate. The crate deserves rest.
true_dawn.012: I know a cinema with chairs. Terrible chairs. But a lot of them.
true_dawn.013: Sold. I'm sold. Movie night. What are we watching?
true_dawn.015: He says it like he's testing whether the sentence holds weight. It does. Everyone hears it hold.
true_dawn.016: Hamin slides a cup across the table toward you without looking up. It is, of course, exactly right.
true_dawn.017: Less ice. They put too much.
true_dawn.018: I asked them to cool it a bit. You burn your tongue.
true_dawn.020: They had grape. Don't ask how.
true_dawn.021: "You're going to have to stop doing that. It's unsettling."
true_dawn.025: It is. He knows it is. He drinks his own coffee to avoid saying so.
true_dawn.026: Take the cup and clink it gently against his.
true_dawn.028: Okay. Okay okay okay. Everyone. Phones out. Not a photo — I've had enough photos — just, everybody put next week in.
true_dawn.031: Eight phones come out around three tables in a kimbap shop at ten to seven in the morning. Nobody's going anywhere. Nobody's leaving in spring.
true_dawn.032: Outside the window, the city wakes up without any idea what it missed.
true_dawn.033: You stayed until morning. Turns out that's the trick. You just keep doing it.
true_dawn.034: Later, someone will ask how you all met. It's going to take a while to explain.
true_dawn.035: "It's a long story," you'll say. "It's a good one."
friendship_route.001: *Stay with everyone.* It comes out simpler than you expected.
friendship_route.002: Like it was the answer the whole time, and just needed saying in a room with people in it.
friendship_route.003: Correct answer. Ding ding ding. No notes.
friendship_route.004: Everyone! We get everyone! That's the best answer! That's the most answer!
friendship_route.006: He has the notebook out. Seven people groan in perfect unison.
friendship_route.008: Everyone is already moving towards the stairs.
friendship_route.009: Why does everyone listen to him and not me?
friendship_route.010: I don't say much. So it counts more.
friendship_route.011: That's so unfair. That's so unfair and so correct.
friendship_route.012: Justin and I will do one more store run. One more! The last one! We'll meet you up there!
friendship_route.013: I'm going to steal everything he buys. For balance.
friendship_route.014: On the way up, you pass the Hall of Doors. It's dim now. Eight doors stand open, their symbols gone soft and grey, like chalk after rain.
friendship_route.015: At the end of the corridor, where there used to be only wall, a ninth door stands open too.
friendship_route.016: It's weird. Like a practice room after everyone's gone home.
friendship_route.017: It's nice, though. Everything that was in there… it's out here now.
friendship_route.018: The rooftop door sticks, and then gives, and then the whole sky is there.
friendship_route.019: The rain has washed Mapo clean. The streets below are wet and orange. Above them, the kind of stars Seoul almost never lets you see.
friendship_route.020: Someone drags up the blankets from the lobby. Someone else brings the cushions from Charlie's fort, which he insists on rebuilding at once.
friendship_route.021: Fort two. Rooftop edition. Now with sky.
friendship_route.022: Twelve minutes later, Hyunjun and Justin come through the door with two bags each, out of breath.
friendship_route.023: They are arguing about whether shrimp crackers are "a snack" or "a lifestyle."
friendship_route.024: Right behind them, there is a knock on the rooftop door, and a delivery rider in a helmet holding a warm, heavy bag.
friendship_route.025: Tteokbokki. From the twenty-four-hour place in Hapjeong. I ordered at 03:51.
friendship_route.027: It's been a long night. I've been learning. I cut every step except the one that mattered.
friendship_route.028: Tteokbokki *and* convenience store! Both! Both is a food group! I said this hours ago!
friendship_route.029: It becomes a feast on a blanket: rice cakes too hot to eat, ramen going soft, kimbap, chips, a bag of tangerines nobody remembers buying.
friendship_route.030: {{playerName}}. I got you something. Don't make it a thing.
friendship_route.031: A triangle kimbap. Tuna mayo. The correct answer, he told you hours ago, when you picked one out of his bag. He remembered.
friendship_route.032: A carton of banana milk, straw already stuck to the side. The one you rescued from Justin, hours ago. He remembered.
friendship_route.033: An ice cream bar, a little soft from the run up the stairs. Rain or not, hours ago, that was your pick. He remembered.
friendship_route.034: A little of everything, all in a pile, as if he couldn't decide and refused to have to.
friendship_route.035: It's a thing. I know. I made it a thing.
friendship_route.036: Hamin sits down next to you and slides a can along the blanket until it touches your hand. He doesn't comment on it. He doesn't need to.
friendship_route.037: Can I have the corner piece of tteokbokki? The burnt one. I want it. I'm saying that out loud.
friendship_route.038: Haruta wants something! Everybody, silence! Give the man the burnt one!
friendship_route.040: Recipients. May I ask what this activity is called?
friendship_route.044: Noted. I have created a new category.
friendship_route.045: Okay. Game. Because I physically cannot help it.
friendship_route.046: "Most likely to." I say a thing, everyone points at who it is. No arguing. Only pointing.
friendship_route.047: Most likely to still be awake at five a.m.
friendship_route.048: Eight fingers point at Daniel. Daniel points at the rooftop speaker.
friendship_route.049: ECHO. Obviously. It's literally its job.
friendship_route.050: Until 05:00. Then I will be asleep. I will not be pointing at anyone.
friendship_route.051: Most likely to cry at the group photo.
friendship_route.052: Everyone points at Hyunjun. Hyunjun, after a moment of dignified consideration, points at himself.
friendship_route.053: That's fair. That's completely fair. I'm going to cry at it tomorrow as well.
friendship_route.054: Most likely to make a schedule for the group chat.
friendship_route.055: I don't need you to point. I know.
friendship_route.056: Everyone points anyway. Songha points at himself too, a little proudly.
friendship_route.057: Most likely to fall asleep before the game's over.
friendship_route.058: Nobody needs to point. Charlie is already asleep, curled inside Fort Two, holding a tangerine.
friendship_route.060: He stops. It's too close to something. The rooftop goes quiet for half a second, and everyone is very carefully not looking at you.
friendship_route.061: No. Scratch that. New one. Most likely to *come back*.
friendship_route.062: Eight fingers, one after the other, point at you.
friendship_route.064: It feels like signing something. It feels like a promise that you want to keep.
friendship_route.065: Unanimous! First unanimous vote of the night!
friendship_route.066: Point at Daniel. "You're coming back for the claw machine."
friendship_route.067: …I *am* coming back for the claw machine. That's an accurate point. I respect it.
friendship_route.069: Then I'll come back for the new claw machine.
friendship_route.070: Point at all of them, one by one.
friendship_route.071: It takes a while. Nobody interrupts. When you reach the last one, Hanbi is smiling at his shoes.
friendship_route.072: After the food, the rooftop goes horizontal. Nine people lying on blankets, looking up, trading half-sentences with the sky.
friendship_route.073: Charlie falls asleep for eleven minutes and wakes up in the middle of an argument about which constellation is shaped like a ladle.
friendship_route.074: You get up to stretch. Somehow that turns into going round the roof, one person at a time.
friendship_route.078: He lifts one side of his coat, and waits. Not assuming. Just offering.
friendship_route.079: You nod. He puts it round your shoulders and goes back to looking at the sky like nothing happened.
friendship_route.080: I didn't use to ask. I just used to move people out of the wind. I'm trying to ask now.
friendship_route.081: I've decided something. I'm staying up here until the power goes. Not because everyone is.
friendship_route.082: Because I want to. That's the whole reason. It's strange how good that feels to say.
friendship_route.084: I want to. There. Twice in one night. Somebody should write it down.
friendship_route.085: Justin is sitting on the ledge-side bench, not dancing. His fingers tap on his knee: five, six, seven, eight.
friendship_route.086: I'm not doing a bit, by the way. Right now. This is just me.
friendship_route.087: It's quieter than I thought. Being just me. It's… okay, actually.
friendship_route.089: Don't tell anyone. I have a reputation.
friendship_route.090: Songha has put the notebook face down on the blanket. He points up at a star, very confidently.
friendship_route.093: It is tonight. I've decided. No plan, no research. Just Gerald.
friendship_route.095: No idea. I'll look it up. Later. Not tonight.
friendship_route.096: Hanbi turns his sketchbook round. Nine tiny figures on a rooftop. One of them is holding a can. One of them is pointing at a star named Gerald.
friendship_route.097: It's rough. I'll fix the hands later.
friendship_route.098: I'm glad you came tonight. {p}That's all. I wanted to say it out loud.
friendship_route.099: I hate this part. The part where you can see the end coming.
friendship_route.100: But it's still happening. Right now. And after it's over, it'll still have happened. That's… that's something, right?
friendship_route.102: Okay. Yeah. I'm writing that on my hand.
friendship_route.103: Where are you going after this?
friendship_route.104: Home. I think. Wherever that is this month.
friendship_route.105: Wherever the snacks are. That's the rule. You made that one up, you know. Years ago.
friendship_route.106: There are so many snacks up here. So technically you're home.
friendship_route.107: Daniel is lying flat on his back with his arms spread out, doing nothing at all.
friendship_route.108: I haven't planned anything for the next ten minutes. No game. Nothing.
friendship_route.109: It's terrifying. It's fine. It's actually really fine.
friendship_route.110: You lie down next to him. Neither of you says anything for a while. He doesn't fill it.
friendship_route.114: The sky goes from black to the deep blue that comes just before the deep blue that comes before morning.
friendship_route.115: Across the rooftops, one window lights up. Someone else in Mapo is awake, making coffee, starting a day. It feels like being waved at.
friendship_route.116: Justin and Hyunjun are sharing the last bag of shrimp crackers. Nobody is stealing. It is, as Hyunjun says, historic.
friendship_route.117: What's everyone doing tomorrow? Honestly. Not the schedule.
friendship_route.118: Sleeping until two. Then eating. Then sleeping.
friendship_route.119: Then it's your turn. You have moved house more times than you can count on both hands. You know exactly what you usually say next.
friendship_route.120: "I think I'm going to stay. In this city. For a while."
friendship_route.121: It's the first time you've said it out loud. It sounds truer outside your head than it did in it.
friendship_route.122: Then I'm adding you to the schedule. Permanently. You can't unsubscribe.
friendship_route.123: "Unpacking. There are boxes in my room I've been ignoring for a month."
friendship_route.124: We'll help. Nine people can unpack anything. We'll make it a game.
friendship_route.125: He will actually make it a game.
friendship_route.126: …Then I guess I'm staying long enough to unpack.
friendship_route.127: "Maybe I'll stay." Say it quietly. Only the sky has to hear.
friendship_route.128: It isn't only the sky. Hamin hears it. You can tell because he doesn't turn his head, and because he smiles.
friendship_route.130: Please come down to the lobby. I have one question. And then I have to go.
friendship_route.132: We'll come back up. After. Come on.
friendship_route.133: Nine people fold up the blankets badly and go down the stairs together, slower than they need to.
friendship_ending.002: I have checked. There is no record of tonight. Nobody submitted one. It has not had time to become old yet.
friendship_ending.003: Daniel is already digging in his pocket. He pulls out a square of expired instant film, a little bent at one corner.
friendship_ending.004: Daniel is already digging through the front desk drawer, and comes up with the old instant camera and a single square of film.
friendship_ending.005: Then here. Scan this. It's the only record we've got.
friendship_ending.006: He lays it on the glass of the terminal. Nine people, badly framed, laughing at something none of them can remember.
friendship_ending.009: OWNERS: HANBI. HAMIN. SONGHA. CHARLIE. HYUNJUN. HARUTA. JUSTIN. DANIEL. {{playerName}}.
friendship_ending.011: For six years, every record I kept had someone missing from it. Someone I could not name.
friendship_ending.012: This one has nobody missing. I did not know a record could look like this.
friendship_ending.013: In the terminal's slot, a card of glass begins to glow. The photograph surfaces inside it slowly, like something rising through water.
friendship_ending.014: It comes out warm. Somehow it comes out warm.
friendship_ending.015: I said I'd cry at it. I'm crying at it. Nobody look at me.
friendship_ending.017: I know! It's fine! It's a happy one!
friendship_ending.018: Okay, but who keeps it? There's one card. There are nine of us.
friendship_ending.019: A rotation. A week each. And before anyone says no—
friendship_ending.020: Nobody says no. For the first time all night, nobody says no to the schedule.
friendship_ending.021: …Oh. Okay. Wow. It feels different when people agree.
friendship_ending.023: You're the one who always leaves, right? So if you have it, you have to come back. To hand it over. That's the rule.
friendship_ending.024: Eight people look at you. Nobody is teasing. It's the way people look at someone when they're handing them something that matters.
friendship_ending.025: "Then I'll come back. That's a promise."
friendship_ending.026: It's in the schedule now. Songha wrote it down. It's legally binding.
friendship_ending.027: "One week, and then I'm fighting Songha for a second week."
friendship_ending.029: Take the card in both hands, and hold it like it might still be warm tomorrow.
friendship_ending.030: It is. You don't know that yet. But it is.
friendship_ending.031: The Archive Wall has begun to dim, box by box, from the top down. Nobody needs to be told what that means.
friendship_ending.032: Thanks for keeping my stuff, ECHO. Even the embarrassing stuff.
friendship_ending.033: Thank you. Really. It was a good screening.
friendship_ending.034: Sleep well, okay? You earned it. Best building ever.
friendship_ending.035: You kept the light on for a long time. Somebody should notice that. {p}We noticed.
friendship_ending.036: Afterwards, without the lights, the building is just a building. You climb the stairs by phone torch, all nine of you, back to the roof.
friendship_ending.037: The sky over Mapo has gone the colour of peach tea left out overnight. Somewhere, a bus is starting its first route.
friendship_ending.038: My phone's dead. Again. Does anyone—
friendship_ending.039: Hanbi hands him the battery pack without looking. The battery pack does a full lap of the roof before it comes back to him, with a little less charge.
friendship_ending.040: New schedule. Nothing until noon. That's it. That's the whole schedule.
friendship_ending.043: Numbers! Everyone! I'm making a group chat. It's called "Stuck-in-a-Talking-Building Friends."
friendship_ending.044: I'm renaming it "Ghost and Eight Others."
friendship_ending.045: I'm pinning a schedule to it. Don't mute it.
friendship_ending.046: Your phone buzzes once. Then eight more times, in a row, like a small applause.
friendship_ending.047: Nine names in a list. You have never been in a group chat you didn't leave within a year. You look at this one for a long moment.
friendship_ending.048: Then, one at a time, they take your phone and save themselves into it properly.
friendship_ending.049: Songha saves himself as "Songha (schedule)." Daniel saves himself as "Daniel ★ Leader ★" and Justin changes it to "Daniel" before the phone comes back.
friendship_ending.050: Hanbi's contact has no note at all. Just his name, and a small drawing of a pencil where the photo would go.
friendship_ending.051: I saved myself as "Charlie (youngest, not my fault)." For legal reasons.
friendship_ending.052: The sun comes up over the rooftops of Mapo.
friendship_ending.053: Nine people stand at the edge of a building that won't exist next week, squinting at it like it's the first sunrise ever made.
friendship_ending.054: Nobody says anything clever. Hyunjun is still crying a bit. Justin is doing one slow, silly spin. Haruta is humming something that isn't from any film.
friendship_ending.055: That would be a good last shot. If this were a film.
friendship_ending.056: It isn't the last one, though.
friendship_ending.058: The glass card is in your coat pocket. You keep touching it, the way you check for keys. It is still, somehow, a little warm.
friendship_ending.059: Down in the alley, a van pulls up. Renovation crew. It's time to go.
friendship_ending.060: Breakfast? Right now? There's a place by the station that does—
friendship_ending.061: Next week. It's on the schedule. Go home, sleep.
friendship_ending.062: Next week, then. I'm holding everyone to it. I'm writing it on my other hand.
friendship_ending.063: I'm sleeping until two. Nobody text me until two. Actually, text me. I want the texts.
friendship_ending.065: He says it the way people say it when they mean the next time is already real. Not a door closing. A door propped open with a shoe.
friendship_ending.068: "See you next week. It's on Songha's schedule."
friendship_ending.069: Finally. Someone who reads the schedule.
friendship_ending.070: Hold up the glass card, just a little. Proof.
friendship_ending.072: And then it's everyone at once, overlapping, on the stairs, in the alley, under the laundromat's light.
friendship_ending.073: Text when you get home. So we know.
friendship_ending.074: See you, {{playerName}}. Next week. I'll pick the film, if we watch one. I already know which.
friendship_ending.075: See you! See you! I'm saying it twice so it counts double!
friendship_ending.076: You have always been the one who leaves. You're leaving now, down the stairs, past the laundromat, out into the morning.
friendship_ending.077: But it's different. You know exactly where you're coming back to.
newmem_group.001: A week later. A tteokbokki place two streets over from where Studio 25 used to be. It's loud, it's steaming, and it closes at midnight. Songha has checked.
newmem_group.002: We booked for seven. It's seven-twenty. Where's Hyunjun?
newmem_group.003: He texted "one more stop" forty minutes ago. That's all. Just "one more stop."
newmem_group.004: He's fine. He shared his location. He's… walking in circles near the station.
newmem_group.006: I'm here! I got off one stop early to walk past the old building. It's all scaffolding now. It looks like it's wearing a jacket.
newmem_group.007: Justin takes a fish cake off Hyunjun's plate before he has even sat down.
newmem_group.008: You didn't even wait for me to sit!
newmem_group.010: I'll order. The cheese one, extra rice cakes. I want the cheese one. I decided on the train.
newmem_group.011: Haruta ordered for the table! Everyone, a round of applause!
newmem_group.012: Please don't clap. The whole restaurant is looking.
newmem_group.013: Wait, what's happening? Why is everyone clapping?
newmem_group.015: Hamin slides a peach iced tea across the table to you without a word. The restaurant doesn't even sell peach iced tea. He must have brought it.
newmem_group.016: Hamin slides a hot chocolate across the table to you without a word. The restaurant doesn't even sell hot chocolate. He must have brought it.
newmem_group.017: Hamin slides a grape soda across the table to you without a word. The restaurant doesn't even sell grape soda. He must have brought it.
newmem_group.018: Hamin slides a black coffee across the table to you without a word. The restaurant doesn't even sell coffee. He must have brought it.
newmem_group.019: You were going to forget to drink anything. You always do when it's loud.
newmem_group.020: Hanbi's phone is at ninety-four percent. Everyone else's is under twenty. He puts the charger in the middle of the table like a centrepiece.
newmem_group.021: Okay. Agenda. Item one: whose week is it with the card?
newmem_group.022: Everyone looks at you. The glass card is in your coat pocket. You checked for it three times on the way here.
newmem_group.023: Mine. Still mine. It's been one week exactly.
newmem_group.024: Then you have to hand it over. That was the rule.
newmem_group.025: You put it on the table between the tteokbokki and the charger. Nine people, badly framed, laughing, catching the restaurant light.
newmem_group.026: New rule. Whoever has it next has to host. Which means another dinner. Which means next week. Which means—
newmem_group.027: Which means we just keep doing this forever?
newmem_group.029: By the door, Daniel has found a claw machine the size of a fridge. He has already spent four thousand won on it.
newmem_group.030: It's a different claw machine. It's a *new* claw machine. The old grudge doesn't apply.
newmem_group.032: Five times to a *new* machine. That's a fresh start.
newmem_group.033: The food arrives, too hot and too much. Somebody knocks over a cup. Somebody starts laughing and can't stop.
newmem_group.034: It isn't a memory yet. It's just Tuesday. You stay until they close.
amb_a1_claw.001: This claw machine is rigged. I can feel it.
amb_a1_claw.003: Four. Don't round down to be nice.
amb_a1_charger.001: Does anyone have a charger? I'm at nine percent.
amb_a1_charger.003: Why do you always have one?
amb_a1_schedule.001: We have until five. I'm making a timetable.
amb_a1_schedule.002: Can the timetable have snacks in it?
amb_a1_crackers.003: The ones in your hand, Justin.
amb_a1_turn.001: Hyunjun. The turn from last week. Watch.
amb_a1_wall.001: Wait, what's happening? Why is the wall glowing?
amb_a1_wall.002: It's been glowing for twenty minutes.
amb_a1_coat.003: Put it on the radiator. Please.
amb_a1_flyer.001: This flyer is for a film night. Eight years ago.
amb_a1_flyer.002: Someone should really take it down.
amb_a1_flyer.003: I think it's nice that nobody did.
amb_a1_speakers.001: If it's a speaker array, where are the speakers?
amb_a1_speakers.002: Maybe the building's just like that.
amb_a1_selfie.001: Everyone look mysterious. It's for the atmosphere.
amb_a1_selfie.002: I can't look mysterious. My face won't do it.
amb_a1_selfie.003: Try looking hungry. Basically the same.
amb_a1_sofa.001: This sofa has a spring that bites.
amb_a1_sofa.003: How do you already know that?
amb_a1_rain.003: Anyone can leave. Nobody wants to.
amb_a2e_hum.001: Can anyone else hear the doors humming?
amb_a2e_diagnostic.003: Polite building. I keep saying it.
amb_a2e_hungry.002: You are. You just haven't noticed yet.
amb_a2e_claw.001: Round five. I've studied the claw. It has patterns.
amb_a2e_claw.002: It just picked up nothing again.
amb_a2e_premiss.001: Is it weird that I miss ECHO already?
amb_a2e_stairs.001: The third stair from the top creaks.
amb_a2e_stairs.003: We should warn Daniel. He jumps them.
amb_a2e_eightcount.003: The lobby has the best floor in the building.
amb_a2e_rule.001: I've written "rule one" on every page.
amb_a2e_rule.003: So I never forget it's the rule.
amb_a2e_pocket.003: It's crinkling in the exact shape of jelly.
amb_a2e_quiet.002: It's okay to be quiet sometimes.
amb_a2e_upstairs.001: Wait, what's happening? Is someone going upstairs?
amb_a2e_upstairs.003: Okay. But tell me first next time.
amb_a2e_tea.001: The kettle in the lounge still works.
amb_a2e_strawberry.001: My hair looks like a wet strawberry.
amb_a2l_fort.001: Nobody touch the fort. The fort has rules.
amb_a2l_ghost.003: Then not a ghost. Case closed.
amb_a2l_floor.001: If I lie down, I'm not getting up.
amb_a2l_shoes.001: I've started hiding snacks in my shoes.
amb_a2l_plugged.002: It's already plugged in. By your hand.
amb_a2l_note.001: I keep thinking about her library note.
amb_a2l_note.003: I'd like to be that sure about anything.
amb_a2l_touched.001: I almost had it. The claw touched it.
amb_a2l_card.001: One card. Just one. That's so small.
amb_a2l_hour.001: It's so quiet at this hour.
amb_a2l_hour.002: The vending machine's the loudest thing now.
amb_a2l_hour.003: Like a film, just before the music starts.
amb_a2l_lying.001: Wait, what's happening? Why is everyone lying down?
amb_a2l_lying.002: It's nearly three. This is what three looks like.
amb_a2l_fiveminutes.001: I haven't talked for five whole minutes.
amb_a2l_goodnight.001: ECHO just said "goodnight" to the vending machine.
